column3: The Hebrew leaves Saul’s son unnamed and preserves the image of his hands becoming slack; BSB names Ish-bosheth and says he “lost courage.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “name” and calls the ancestry “sons of Benjamin.”
The Hebrew coordinates this statement with “and”; BSB introduces it with “because.”
The Hebrew refers to him as “he” and describes lying for the midday rest; BSB supplies “the king” and calls it a nap.
The Hebrew describes taking wheat without a separate “as if.”
The Hebrew leaves Ish-bosheth unnamed and explicitly locates the bed in his sleeping chamber.
The Hebrew explicitly adds “and said to them” after David’s answering.
The Hebrew preserves the image of the messenger’s own eyes in his self-assessment.
The Hebrew uses singular “your hand”; BSB has plural “your hands.”
The Hebrew leaves the slain men unnamed and does not explicitly supply “bodies”; BSB names Rechab and Baanah and adds “their bodies.”
